content: A Certified Diabetes Educator (CDE) is a healthcare professional who has specialized training and certification to teach individuals with diabetes how to effectively manage their condition. Typically, a CDE is also a nurse or dietitian who has undergone additional training to develop expertise in diabetes care. To become certified, a diabetes educator must complete formal education, accumulate years of practical experience, and pass a formal examination. In the United States, certification is granted by the National Certification Board for Diabetes Educators, while in Canada, it is awarded by the Canadian Diabetes Association. The role of a CDE is invaluable for individuals who need to acquire the necessary tools and skills to regulate their blood sugar levels and prevent long-term complications associated with hyperglycemia. Unlike an endocrinologist, a CDE can dedicate as much time as needed to a newly diagnosed patient, providing both educational guidance and emotional support.
